title: 先定边界，再让 AI 写
series: The Founder's Playbook - Building an AI-Native Startup
audience: Founders, solo builders, AI startup operators, and technical product leaders

coverGrid.note: Cover crop constraints apply later; this scene graph is for video timing.

visualSystem.styleIntent: reuse Founder Playbook warm decision-gate VI while changing the central artifact to boundary/context discipline
typography: Rounded / humanist Chinese sans stack from the Founder Playbook system
Avenir Next / Inter / system sans for metadata
palette: cyan for evidence and readable context
rose for drift, sprawl, and weak scope
symbolGrammar: Before designing any symbol, identify the section key message. The symbol must encode that takeaway, not merely the section topic or a noun from the narration.
Comply with the locked Founder Playbook VI first; iOS icon discipline is only a secondary reference for silhouette and legibility.
Use abstract concept marks, not literal product UI: boundary frame, signal bars, threshold line, mismatch paths, void state, execution stack.
Fit every symbol to the concept: fast code uses path/stack, scope uses boundary frame, feature creep uses nodes outside the frame, context drift uses crossing paths.
Keep each mark readable at phone size with short labels as anchors.
Use common diagram grammar before invention.
motionPrinciples: One visual focus per voice chunk.
Motion is semantic: code speed, boundary expansion, evidence gate, scope document reveal, context reset, drift warning, decision lock.
Major action sound cues only; no per-animation notification layer.
Subtitles must stay clear of the central boundary diagrams.
Animation order and hold time follow measured voice timing.
frameFittingConstraints: No scene may rely on dense document text for meaning.
Every diagram must remain readable in a phone feed.
Subtitles must not sit in a box or collide with central artifacts.

sourceRefs.role: source value inventory and page-area mapping

sourceFidelityGuardrails: MVP is still evidence-gathering about the solution, not full-product construction.
AI technical debt is framed as context, architecture, and boundary drift, not only bad code.
Scope boundaries must include what the MVP does, does not do, and what evidence justifies adding features.
Return, payment, referral, or repeated use are evidence examples, not a full PMF framework lesson.
Claude-specific artifacts are treated as source examples, not universal product law.
Security/compliance details and launch hardening remain deferred.

soundEffects.rationale: Major opening action: fast execution appears before the boundary rule.
Major concept notification: unclear boundary creates product sprawl.
Major decision action: solve / not solve / evidence-to-add becomes the scope boundary.
Major warning action: code can run while boundary/context drifts.
Major bridge action only: the next episode router gate appears.

episodeClaims: AI coding speed can scatter an unclear product.
After validation, the next risk is uncontrolled building.
MVP is a focused evidence-gathering stage.
Scope is a three-part boundary: solve, not solve, evidence to add.
AI technical debt can compound when product boundaries and architecture context drift.
AI should execute decisions already made, not decide product scope inside each coding session.
